analysis.title: CoTD: A $1.5tn Muse?
key_insights: Meta said it hit major milestones toward personal superintelligence, including the launch of Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, and raised the floor of its 2026 capex guidance to $135-145bn.
Meta shares closed more than 7% below their level before the Q3 2025 results, when a warning of notably larger 2026 spending cut the shares about 11% in a day, their worst fall since 2022.

Bloomberg estimates hyperscaler capex rose from just over $100bn in 2020 to $500bn last year, will approach $1tn this year and will plateau above $1.6tn a year from 2029. The estimate includes big US cloud and platform companies, Chinese hyperscalers and neoclouds.
The stated justification for the spending has moved from better ad targeting to superintelligence.
Meta's Q3 revenue rose 26% y/y, average ad prices rose 14%, and Muse reached 10 million users in six weeks. Free cash flow turned negative in Q3.

The report says the open question is whether superintelligence arrives fast enough to justify about $1.5tn of annual capex, and who bears the cost if it does not. Demand still outstrips supply and capability gains raise the prospect of recursive self-improvement.
Strong AI equity performance over the past year has broadly shifted from the companies spending on capex to the companies receiving that spending (per Monday's CoTD).
earnings_insights: Meta Q3 2026 (reported 10/21): revenue +26% y/y, average ad prices +14%, free cash flow negative. 2026 capex guidance floor raised to $135-145bn.
risk_factors: Free cash flow at Meta turned negative in Q3 as capex rises.
Destination, timing and economics of superintelligence remain deeply uncertain, and it is unclear who is left holding the bill if it arrives too slowly to justify about $1.5tn of annual capex.
